nodes.description: U5 loop I base-pairs with the last nucleotides of the upstream exon, contributing to 5' splice-site selection, and holds both exons in register for exon ligation. A variant U5 snRNA incorporated into spliceosomes is expected to change which exon-boundary sequences pair well with loop I. Whether the mutant snRNA acts by dominant negative or altered-function effect, rather than by loss of function, has not been tested.

nodes.description: A heterozygous de novo single-nucleotide substitution or small insertion in a roughly 8-nucleotide stretch (about n.37 to n.44) of RNU5B-1 that encodes the invariant 5' loop I of U5 snRNA. The stretch is depleted of variation in gnomAD and UK Biobank but not variant-free: a different substitution, n.39C>T, is present in three gnomADv4 individuals. Recurrent variants are n.39C>G, n.42_43insA and n.44A>G. RNU5B-1 and RNU5A-1 are the main U5 genes expressed in brain.

nodes.description: Alternative to target-specific mis-splicing. Cellular quality-control pathways degrade defective snRNAs, including disease-mutant snRNAs, before they assemble into spliceosomes; when that control fails, defective snRNAs form aberrant spliceosomes that alter splicing. Applied to RNU5B-1, a loop I variant could either lower the amount of functional U5B snRNP or, if it escapes degradation, impair spliceosomes broadly rather than redirect them to a defined target set. This has been shown for U4-2 mutants, not for U5 variants, and neither the level nor the spliceosome incorporation of mutant U5B-1 has been measured.

nodes.description: In cultured lymphocytes from six individuals with U5 variants (four RNU5B-1), the variants did not reproduce the 5' splice-site signature of ReNU syndrome and shared no common 5' or 3' splice-site signature with each other. Analysed one at a time, RNU5B-1 n.39C>G possibly altered mainly 5' splice-site usage and n.44A>G mainly 3' splice-site usage; the authors call these possible variant-specific effects. The affected genes, and which events matter in brain, are not known.
